title: Username From Email
statement:
Suggest a username for every account, taken from its email address.

The `users` table has one row per account:

- `id`: the account's id, unique
- `email`: the account's email address, with exactly one `@`

Some addresses were typed with capital letters. Return each account's `id` and a `username` column, ordered by `id`. The username is the part of the email before the `@`, in lowercase.

Expected output:

```text
 id |   username
----+--------------
  1 | maria.lopez
  2 | jsmith
  3 | dev_kim42
  4 | olivia.brown
  5 | sam
(5 rows)
```

tests.output:
id |   username
----+--------------
  1 | maria.lopez
  2 | jsmith
  3 | dev_kim42
  4 | olivia.brown
  5 | sam
(5 rows)

id |   username
----+---------------
  1 | maria.lopez
  2 | jsmith
  3 | dev_kim42
  4 | olivia.brown
  5 | sam
  6 | noah.williams
  7 | a
(7 rows)

tests.stdin: UPDATE users SET email = 'Maria.Garcia+news@example.com' WHERE id = 1;
tests.output:
id |     username
----+-------------------
  1 | maria.garcia+news
  2 | jsmith
  3 | dev_kim42
  4 | olivia.brown
  5 | sam
(5 rows)

tests.stdin:
DELETE FROM users WHERE id > 2;
INSERT INTO users (id, email) VALUES (3, 'Team-Lead@office.dev');
tests.output:
id |  username
----+-------------
  1 | maria.lopez
  2 | jsmith
  3 | team-lead
(3 rows)

hints: `split_part(text, delimiter, n)` splits a string on a delimiter and returns piece number `n`, counting from 1.
`lower` turns every letter of a string into lowercase.

sql.starter:
-- TODO: keep only the part before the @, in lowercase
SELECT id, email AS username
FROM users
ORDER BY id;
sql.solution:
SELECT
  id,
  lower(split_part(email, '@', 1)) AS username
FROM users
ORDER BY id;
